title: Silver Cross Window
subject: Criminal Law & Procedure
stem:
Esther decided to steal a small silver cross necklace that belonged to Lydia. Esther knew where Lydia kept the necklace because she had been in Lydia’s house after Bible-study dinners when Lydia took off the necklace and placed it in a jewelry box on the bathroom counter. One night, Esther went to Lydia’s house. Lydia was away, and the house was dark. Esther opened the bathroom window, saw the jewelry box on the counter, and started to climb inside. As one leg cleared the window sill, Lydia’s dog began barking loudly. Terrified, Esther jumped back outside and ran away.

The crimes below are listed in descending order of seriousness. What is the most serious crime, if any, committed by Esther?
call: The crimes below are listed in descending order of seriousness. What is the most serious crime, if any, committed by Esther?
rightExplanation:
A is correct. Esther committed burglary because the decisive fact is not whether she got fully inside or stole the necklace. The decisive fact is that she crossed the window line with part of her body while intending to steal.

Gold Key: For burglary-entry questions, a partial entry is enough. Any part of the body crossing into the protected space can satisfy entry. The intended felony does not need to be completed.

Silver Key: Read this answer array as a seriousness ladder. Once the completed higher crime is present, do not stop at a lesser attempt answer.

c3.label: CUT
c3.text: D is cut after the Gold Key because “No crime” cannot stand once partial entry with theft intent is recognized.

c3.label: CLASH
c3.text: A and B clash on one axis: completed entry or mere attempt. The fact that resolves it is “one leg cleared the window sill.” The Gold Key tells the student that this is enough entry.

c3.label: CALL
c3.text: C falls under the seriousness-ladder Silver Key. Attempted larceny is lower and not responsive once burglary is established.

studentScript: They ask most serious. A/B fight on completed burglary versus attempt. The leg crossed the sill. Gold Key: partial entry counts. Pick burglary.

A.signal: Highest crime on the ladder once the Gold Key turns the leg-over-sill fact into entry.
A.lawyer: Burglary is satisfied because Esther broke and entered Lydia's dwelling at night with intent to steal; partial body entry suffices.

B.signal: B answers the neighboring attempt frame after the completion fact has already crossed the threshold.
B.lawyer: Attempted burglary is not the most serious crime because the burglary was completed at entry.

C.signal: C focuses on the intended theft rather than the highest completed crime.
C.lawyer: Attempted larceny is lower than burglary and is not the most serious crime once burglary is established.

D.signal: D cannot survive once the Gold Key recognizes partial entry plus theft intent.
D.lawyer: At minimum the facts show criminal attempt conduct; under the tested rule they show completed burglary.

goldKeys.statement: For burglary-entry questions, any part of the body crossing into the protected space can be enough entry; full-body entry and completed theft are not required.
goldKeys.trigger: a hand, foot, leg, tool, or other part crosses a doorway/window line before the actor flees
goldKeys.unlocks: the completed burglary vs attempted burglary trap
goldKeys.authority: lawyer_confirmation_only: common-law burglary sources and partial-entry case law

silverKeys.statement: When the call says the crimes are listed in descending seriousness, pick the highest crime that is actually completed; do not stop at a lower attempt answer.
silverKeys.trigger: answer choices are offense labels ordered from more serious to less serious

remediation.title: Partial Entry Beats Attempt
remediation.signal: window/door boundary crossed by one body part, followed by flight
remediation.studentMove: Name the completion axis: entry or no entry. Then use the seriousness ladder.
remediation.tinyRule: Body part inside = entry; completed burglary outranks attempted burglary.
remediation.trap: Stopping at attempted burglary because the actor fled before fully entering.
